analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (documentation only, lines 1243-1617 of a file whose head grew to about 400 added lines at the top). No executable code, configuration, or threat-model file changes appear in the supplied evidence, so no direct security regression is observable here. I read the entries for security-relevant claims that later review passes should check against the real source diffs, which were not supplied:

(1) Cluster prefix cache per tenant (lines ~1401-1403, 1445). The changelog claims prefix keys and SSD records now carry a SHA-256 digest of the cache scope, and that requests without a cache scope keep nothing. That is consistent with T-041 and SEC-035. Whether the digest is folded into the HMAC lookup tag, as T-041(d) requires, cannot be confirmed. Local-endpoint requests carry no partition and keep the earlier shared behavior.
(2) The model-copy path over the Thunderbolt cable (line 1342) is said to use encrypted records, a digest-pinned manifest, and rejection of hard links, unexpected files, and occupied destinations. Those controls need verification in the source.
(3) Cluster serving without a coordinator (lines 1260-1262) binds the local API to all interfaces by default, with a shared API key. This widens network exposure to LAN or tailnet. It is documented, and --bind can restrict it. It is new attack surface that the threat model does not cover and that the source should confirm.
(4) Pair-serving grants and the declared public-model qualifications (lines 1323-1326, 1525-1527) rest on owner decisions with limited evidence, as the changelog itself admits. This relates to T-052 and T-054, and is a policy matter rather than a code defect.
(5) Packed, quantized SSD prefix records (lines 1580-1582) change the at-rest format. The AAD, HMAC naming, and TTL are claimed unchanged. T-041 would need an update if the metadata fields changed.
(6) The KEK and weight-hash reads with F_NOCACHE, and the new environment-variable diagnostics, are not security relevant on their face.

No finding is raised because the excerpts are prose only. The next pass should review the actual cluster, SSD-cache, and local-API bind source changes.
